steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
Sift together flour, baking soda, and salt in a medium bowl; set aside.
Cream together butter, peanut butter, 1/2 cup white sugar, and brown sugar in a large bowl until smooth. Beat in egg, then stir in vanilla. Gradually blend in flour mixture until combined.
Shape dough into 1-inch balls. Roll in 1/2 cup white sugar, then place 2 inches apart on ungreased cookie sheets. Use fork times to make a crisscross pattern on each dough ball.
Bake in the preheated oven until edges are set, 10 to 12 minutes. Cool slightly, then remove cookies to a wire rack to cool completely.

raw_recipe.headline: Peanut Butter Cookies
raw_recipe.description: A very delicious peanut butter cookie recipe that is easy to make. These cookies stay soft in an airtight container. For special occasions, press five peanut halves into the top before baking.
raw_recipe.name: Peanut Butter Cookies

review.reviewBody: Ok, I am angry. I wanted desert. It was cold outside. I didn't want to go out so I made something. This. And it was good. Now I know that I can bake, I am going to get fat. Seriously - really good cookies and I don't even like peanut butter. It was just the only thing in the house that could be turned into a cookie (my husband likes it). PS: I didn't roll them in sugar - I ran out, but I did sprinkle a little confectioner's sugar on top once they were done. Pretty.

These were very good, I followed recipe. Cookies are kind of medium peanut butter in taste . I like cookies any way so I was happy with them.. The only thing I noticed was the bottoms of mine were starting to burn at 8 mins. I tried a few things since there was enough dough to make small batches and adjustments. First I chilled all the dough I used but, my first batch at 8 mins was pretty close to burnt. Two was play with the size, and three was turn the oven down about 10 degrees and use an insulated baking sheet and regular baking sheet. My best batch used the insulated baking sheet at 8 mins, any size and they came out perfect.

I made these and rolled the dough into a log to slice off and bake. Super soft and yummy only thing I did different was that I added extra peanut butter...Also I like smooth not crunchy so thats what I used. Absolutely a keeper. Hubby loved them as he does anything peanutbuttery.

These are just like the peanut butter cookies my dad always made! I did make a couple changes:
- I didn't roll them in sugar. They don't need the extra sweetness, in my opinion - but maybe that was because I used Skippy peanut butter, which has added sugar already.
- I only baked them for 8 minutes. Overbaked peanut butter cookies are the worst. Even then, they were close to being too dark on the bottoms. 

Also, be sure to space them apart on the baking sheet. These cookies spread out more than you think they will.

I’ve been looking for a better pb cookie for a while now. This one is light and chewy. I doubled the recipe and added an extra egg with a bit of cinnamon (I believe cinnamon enhances the flavors) along with a cup of chocolate chips. I also only cooked 8 min. If you like a crunchier cookie, do the full time as stated. These will be my go to pb cookies from now on!

Best peanut butter cookies I've ever made, and probably ever had before. My husband likes them. I didnt bother sprinkling sugar on top. They were sweet without it. I did put one Ghiraldi natural White chocolate chip on the top of each cookie after I forked them down. 375 seemed like it was a little too hot for my oven. I took them out at 10 mins and they were well browned on the bottom, but soft on top. A couple more minutes may have burned the bottoms. Oh, yes and I used white whole wheat flour and Florida Crystals sugar instead of white sugar and an energy egg replacer instead of real egg. I replace with those in all my baked goods. Yum, Yum....

Fabulous pnutty cookie!!! Of course, being the baker that I am, there were some changes made, but only for my preference... First off, I did not roll in sugar... just not my thing. Secondly, I added 1 cup of creamy pnutty, 3/4 brwn sgr, and 2 tsp nilla. And finally, I played with baking times a bit... 8 min gave a super soft, little gewy center. 10 min on metal pan gave a perfect soft nutty cookie. 12 min on baking stone gave the same as the metal pan. I used the pumpkin stencil of my cookie press, which produced fantastic holiday cookies!! (the batter is PERFECT consistency for successful stencils) Will absolutely be using this as my "go-to" pnutty cookie recipe!

I have made this recipe countless times. Always comes out good. I used my mini muffin tins, sprayed them with Joy baking spray, spooned cookie dough in to them and baked as directed in recipe. When they come out of oven, I filled the depression that forms with jelly or preserves. Just a twist on the classic peanut butter cookies.

Delicious peanut butter cookies with a twist, I used sugar free ingredients. The first time I made it, it only made about 24 small cookies. I made it again but the second time, I doubled the recipe & made it with sugar free ingredients. I added 3/4 cup of extra peanut butter. I used Splenda brown sugar & white sugar. I rolled the balls in regular sugar so it didn’t have the sugar free taste to it. My husband loved them!
I found that 9 minutes in the oven makes a perfect cookie, soft and chewy with crispy edges. Even at 10 minutes, their delicious!

Wonderful simple and delicious recipe. I made some modifications as suggested. I added extra 1/2 cup of flour and peanut butter. About 4 tablespoons of heavy whipping cream and water mixed together. I place though in the freezer for 10 minutes. I made 1/2 of the batch with cocoa powder, and added confectioner sugar on top of cookies. Baked for 9 minutes.
So delicious! Accidentally used salted butter but it turned out great!
These were the best tasting PB cookies ever. Everyone that tried them thought the same.

These were delicious!!! The flavor is wonderful, it turned out beautiful, and ultimately these are well worth a bake as-is! I've never made peanut butter cookies before, and these ones were perfect for most of us. My ONE complaint is I'm trying to make softer cookies than this, because one of my loved ones doesn't have upper teeth. I think I can tweak it with a little less time in the oven or perhaps a lower temperature.
This is my all time favorite recipe growing up. Had a sweet tooth and it was really good.
These were the best peanut butter cookies I’ve made. Thanks for sharing!
These cookies have become a favorite for our family of four. I love the fact that they stay very soft & chewy in a tupperware container. And .. so good!
